newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul says North Korean economy keeps shrinking.
newsitem.headline: Seoul says North Korean economy keeps shrinking.

text.p: North Korea's economy shrank for the seventh year running in 1996, when harvests met just over half the nation's needs, the South Korean government said on Thursday.
A report by the National Unification Ministry, which monitors North Korea, said there were no signs of recovery for the communist economy, which contracted by an estimated three percent last year.
Seoul officials said poor farming equipment, shortage of fertilisers and the lack of incentives for farmers pushed the Stalinist state closer to famine.
"There's no hope for the North Korean economy without a massive blood transfusion," said Hong Song-kuk, a director at the ministry.

"But you have to make sure the patient has the same blood type before starting any transfusion. Unless North Korea reforms its economy and opens its door, Western aid will not end its woes," Hong said.

The report said North Korea's food harvest totalled 3.69 million tonnes last year, up from 3.45 million tonnes from 1995 but below the average annual crop of 4.14 million tonnes in the past seven years.
Hong said the estimate by the United Nations' World Food Programme (WFP) of a 2.3 million-tonne food shortage in North Korea this year was conservative.
"North Korea's annual grain needs amount to some 6.7 million tonnes. Last year's crops leave North Korea short of about three million tonnes," he said.

South Korean officials said that apart from floods, which damaged an estimated 1.5 million tonnes of harvests in 1995 and one million tonnes in 1995, North Korea had suffered from a chronic shortage of about two million tonnes of grain per year in the past four years.

Catherine Bertini, WFP executive director, said on Tuesday after a trip to North Korea that the presence of thin, lethargic children there indicated that a famine could strike the impoverished state as early as this month.

An influential South Korean newspaper on Wednesday quoted North Korean leader Kim Jong-il as saying anarchy could soon reign in his nation because of an acute food shortage that has even hit the military.
Kim held Communist Party and government officials responsible for "a state of anarchy being created because of food problems today", the Chosun Ilbo said.
The daily, reputed to have many sources within the Seoul government, said Kim made the remarks in a speech on December 7 in Pyongyang.
"People are found everywhere scrounging for food," Kim was quoted as saying. "Stations and trains are crowded with people looking for food. You see heartbreaking scenes everywhere."
The unification ministry report said the bulk of North Korea's production facilities were idle because of an energy shortage. Fewer than 30 percent of plants in the nation were in operation in 1996.
Seoul officials said the scarcity of foreign currency prevented Pyongyang from buying energy and production equipment needed to make goods, which in turn further limited sources of hard currency.
Pyongyang's foreign trade totalled $1.07 billion in 1996, down 5.3 percent from the previous year, the report said.
